title: Identification of phosphorylation site on PARP1 mediating its cytosolic translocation in virus-infected HeLa cells
protocol: Propagate HSV-1 viruses and measure the titers of virus by TCID50 assay on Vero cells.
Store the virus at −80°C for 2–4 years.
Infect HeLa cells with HSV-1 (MOI = 1) for indicated time.
Seed HeLa cells in 15 mm glass bottom cell culture dishes.
At 70%–80% confluency, infect cells with HSV-1 (MOI = 1) for 4 h.
Discard the culture medium and wash cells twice with sterile 1× phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Fix the cells with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) for 10–20 min at 25°C.
Wash cells three times with 1× PBS.
Treat cells with 1× permeabilization buffer for 5 min at 25°C.
Block cells with 1% BSA for 30 min at 25°C.
Dilute the PARP1 antibody in QuickBlock Primary antibody diluent at a ratio of 1:100.
Add the diluted PARP1 antibody to the dish and incubate for 12 hours at 4°C.
Wash cells three times with 1×PBS.
Incubate cells with 1 mL of secondary antibody (goat anti-Rabbit Alex Fluor594) diluted 1:1,000 in 1% BSA for 1 hour at 25°C in the dark.
Incubate cells with 200 μL DAPI Staining Solution for 5 to 10 minutes at 25°C in the dark.
Wash cells three times with 1×PBS.
Add 1 mL of antifade mounting medium.
Collect images using a Leica TCS SP8 confocal laser microscopy system with a 63× oil immersion objective.
Determine PARP1 localization in cells from different dishes.
Take photos of ten different microscopic fields.
Analyze DAPI signal to identify the nucleus.
Use ImageJ software (version 1.8.0.172) for signal segmentation and analysis.
Carry out further data analysis using GraphPad Prism 8 software.
Ensure experiments are representative of three independent trials.
Avoid dish drying when washing with PBS or adding reagents in all steps to prevent experimental failure or misleading information collection.
Seed HeLa cells in 6-well plates at approximately 1 × 10^6 cells per well.
Culture the seeded cells for 24 hours to reach 70-80% confluency.
Collect cells from two wells as one sample for cytoplasmic and nuclear fractionation.
Wash collected cells twice with 1× PBS in a 1.5 mL reaction tube.
Centrifuge at 120 × g for 5 minutes, then remove the supernatant completely.
Add 40 μL of protease inhibitor cocktail (prepared by dissolving one tablet in 2 mL PBS) and 1 μL of 1 M DTT to every 1 mL of Buffer A before use.
Add 150-200 μL of Buffer A supplemented with protease inhibitor cocktail and DTT to the cell pellet, place on ice for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge at 15,000 × g for 6 minutes.
Transfer the supernatant to a pre-cooled 1.5 mL reaction tube; this is the cytoplasmic extract.
Wash the pellets five times with 500 μL wash buffer supplemented with protease inhibitor cocktail and DTT.
Add protease inhibitor cocktail 40 μL per 1 mL of Buffer B before use.
Add 1 M DTT 1 μL per 1 mL of Buffer B before use.
Add 50-80 μL Buffer B to the pellet.
Vortex the tube at high speed for 10–15 seconds every 10 minutes for a total of 30 minutes, and place it on ice during this period.
Centrifuge the mixture at 15,000 × g for 15-30 minutes to collect the supernatant as nuclear extract.
Denature both cytoplasmic and nuclear fractions in 1× SDS protein loading buffer at 95°C for 8 minutes before western blot analysis.
Membrane transfer: wet transfer.
Transfer the protein to a 0.22 μm pore size nitrocellulose membrane in 1× transfer buffer at 100 V for 1.5 h.
Block the membrane with 5% skim milk or 5% BSA in 1×TBST for 1 h at 25°C.
Dilute the primary antibody in blocking buffer at a 1:1,000 dilution.
Incubate the NC membrane with the primary antibody for 12 h at 4°C on a rotator.
Wash the membrane three times with 1×TBST on a shaker; 10 min each time.
Dilute the secondary antibody in 1×TBST at a 1:5,000 dilution and incubate for 1 h at 25°C.
Wash the membrane three times with 1×TBST.
Expose the gel to Supersignal West Pico developer.
Collect the image data by Amersham Imager 600.
Predict phosphorylation sites in human PARP1 protein sequence from UniProtKB.
Seed HeLa cells in a 10 cm cell culture dish to achieve about 1 × 10^7 cells per well and culture for 24 hours to reach 70-80% confluency.
Infect the cultured HeLa cells with HSV-1 at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 1 for 4 hours.
Wash infected cells twice with 1× PBS.
Lysate the cells using 200 μL RIPA Lysis Buffer supplemented with protease inhibitor cocktail, 1 mM PMSF, and phosphatase inhibitor cocktail.
Place the cell lysate on a shaker at 4°C for 30 minutes to thoroughly lyse the cells.
Centrifuge the lysate at 15,000 × g for 10 minutes and discard the cellular debris.
Wash Protein A/G agarose twice with 1 mL 1×PBS.
Prepare a 50% protein A/G agarose working solution in 1×PBS.
Incubate cell lysates with protein A/G agarose (50 μL) and anti-PARP1 antibody (5 μL) at 4°C for 12 h.
Wash the beads with 1 mL 1× PBST five times, discarding supernatant completely.
Add 30–50 μL 1× protein loading buffer to the beads.
Boil the mixture at 95°C for 10 min.
Subject boiled protein sample to 10% SDS-PAGE gel electrophoresis.
Wash the gel in a sterile 10 cm dish with deionized water, heating and shaking for preparation.
Stain the gel with Coomassie brilliant blue fast staining solution until clear target protein bands appear.
Discard staining solution and wash residual solution off to stop staining reaction.
Take pictures and record the results.
Elute the gel if a background-free picture of the gel is desired.
Add about 100 mL of deionized water to the gel.
Shake the gel on a shaker to decolorize.
Carefully pour off the liquid after 5-15 minutes.
Add another 100 mL of deionized water and continue decolorizing on the shaker.
Repeat steps until background staining is highly reduced, typically requiring 30-120 minutes.
Cut the PARP1 band from the gel after Coomassie brilliant blue staining and elution.
Decolorize the cut PARP1 band thoroughly.
Subject the decolorized PARP1 band to mass spectrometry (MS).
Wash the gel on a rotator in deionized water for a total of 5 minutes, washing 3-5 times.
Shake and wash the gel using boiled deionized water on a shaker for 5 minutes, washing 2-3 times to speed up the process.
Load the sample onto an HPLC chromatography system named Thermo Fisher Easy-nLC 1000 equipped with a C18 column (1.8 mm, 0.15 × 100 mm).
Determine T594 as the phosphorylation site of PARP1.
Reconstitute PARP1 KO HeLa cells with HA, HA-PARP1, or HA-PARP1(T594A) plasmid, respectively.
Seed HeLa cells in a 6-well-plate (about 1 × 10^6 cells/well).
Culture for 24 h to reach 70%–80% confluency.
Infect with HSV-1 at MOI = 1 for 4 h and 8 h, respectively.
Wash cells twice with 1× PBS.
Denature in 1× SDS protein loading buffer at 95°C for 8 min.
Resolve proteins by electrophoresis through a 10% SDS-polyacrylamide gel.
Transfer separated proteins onto PVDF membranes.
Incubate with the anti-phospho-PARP1 T594 antibody.
Apply an enhanced chemiluminescence reagent (Thermo Fisher Scientific) for immunoblotting.
Dilute the anti-phospho-PARP1 T594 antibody at a ratio of 1:500 for use in the assay.
